fields.Front: What is the organizational payoff of conceptual integrity?
fields.Back: It isolates the core complexity of the design, so the rest of the team can focus on implementation without worrying about (or re-litigating) the design decisions.

fields.Front: What is modularization, and how does it relate to encapsulation?
fields.Back: Breaking large systems into smaller, manageable modules, each with a well-defined interface and hidden internal details. It is the same idea as class-level encapsulation, one scale up: a clean interface outside, hidden complexity inside, one coherent vision governing both.

fields.Text: {{c1::Conceptual integrity}} is a consistent and unified vision across the entire project, in which a single {{c1::source}} controls the design decisions so the system's complexity is hidden behind a simpler, unified interface.
fields.Extra: Just as a class in OOP hides its internal workings behind public methods.

fields.Text: {{c1::Modularization}} breaks large systems into smaller manageable modules, each with a {{c1::well-defined interface}} and {{c1::hidden internal details}} - the same idea as class-level encapsulation, one scale up.
